source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured primary references. Current Kubernetes documentation supports volume/PV/PVC lifecycle and binding, access and volume modes, object/deletion protection, expansion, StorageClass defaults/reclaim/binding/topology parameters, dynamic provisioning, StatefulSet identities/update/PVC retention, snapshot CRDs/controller/CSI dependencies, ephemeral-volume ownership, local ephemeral accounting, capacity-aware scheduling, and driver-dependent volume health. Current Kubernetes CSI documentation supports provisioner, attacher, snapshotter, resizer, health-monitor, controller, driver-capability, and compatibility responsibilities. The chapter does not treat Bound PVCs, attached/mounted volumes, StatefulSet replicas, ReadyToUse snapshots, encryption, or retained PVs as proof of application correctness, durability, independence, backup, or recovery.

evidence: Checked S=(D,C,A,P,T,Q,B,R,E,L,O,X), PV/PVC/topology binding, data-position RPO, time-based RTO, usable-state conjunction, replica-zone inequality, and n>=2f+1 notation.
Checked tuple, bidirectional binding, mapping, time/log-position difference, indexed variables, conjunction, inequality, and implication boundaries with repository-compatible GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation distinguishes resource binding, physical topology, application validity, and measured recovery.

evidence: Executed stateful-storage-inventory and reproduced eight claims, six persistent, two ephemeral, five delayed-binding, three Retain, two RWOP, five snapshot-required, and three zones.
Recomputed Retain for orders-data, orders-wal, and registry; RWOP for orders-data and registry; snapshot-required for orders-data, orders-wal, analytics-shared, media, and registry.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture is synthetic and explicitly disclaims real driver, durability, consistency, backup, topology, performance, security, and recovery evidence.

evidence: Expanded the twelve-element stateful binding model through data semantics, consistency, access, provisioning, topology, quality, backup, recovery, security, lifecycle, observation, and exceptions.
Expanded PVC-to-PV-to-topology binding separately from pod/member identity and provider volume identity.
Expanded measured RPO and RTO from acknowledged/recoverable data positions and failure/validated-restoration times, rather than schedules or object readiness.
Expanded the nine-conjunct usable-state predicate and verified that Bound, Attached, Mounted, or ReadyToUse alone is insufficient.
Checked the 2f+1 voting-member lower bound under stated crash-failure/protocol assumptions without equating PVC count or mount count to replicas.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formulas model requirements and evidence boundaries; they do not prove provider durability or protocol correctness.

evidence: Reviewed zero/oversized capacity, inode exhaustion, quotas, attach limits, invalid mount options, expansion retry, unsupported shrink, filesystem versus raw block, and empty or generic ephemeral ownership.

Reviewed immediate wrong-zone binding, delayed binding with nodeName, missing/stale capacity, zone loss, local-volume node loss, co-located replicas, node partitions, stale attachments, force detach, co-node RWO writers, and absent fencing.

Reviewed StatefulSet broken rollout, stale ordinal reuse, unsafe scale-down, PVC retention/reclaim combinations, finalizer removal, orphaned retained PVs, provider cleanup, legal hold, and multi-copy erasure.

Reviewed crash-inconsistent and multi-volume snapshots, same-account/region backups, corrupt/missing logs, lost keys, incompatible drivers, untested full-size restore, compromised storage authority, shared filesystem tenants, and ransomware.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Capacity, topology, split-brain, destructive lifecycle, recovery, security, and governance boundaries are explicit.

evidence: Traced data classification through volume lifetime, claim identity, class selection, delayed binding, attach/mount, filesystem/block use, application recovery, backup, retention, and erasure.
Checked topology and single-writer invariants across scheduler participation, volume reachability, failure-domain independence, access modes, application quorum, epochs/leases, and fencing.

Checked durability and recovery invariants through acknowledged position, replication, application-consistent capture, independent export, integrity, isolated restore, validation, and observed RPO/RTO.

Checked lifecycle, capacity/performance, and security invariants across StatefulSet PVC retention, PV reclaim, snapshot/backup expiry, provider deletion, headroom, rebuild load, all copies, CSI authority, and encryption keys.
invariant_checking.notes: All declared identity, topology, single-writer, durability, recovery, lifecycle, capacity, performance, and security invariants remain consistent across examples and answers.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no new theorem and contains no deductive proof; the standard quorum lower bound is explicitly conditional on protocol assumptions.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; the mechanism is labeled an assurance structure with provider, driver, application, independence, backup, key, and operational assumptions.

evidence: The storage inventory is labeled synthetic and disclaims operational equivalence.
Normative project documentation, practitioner synthesis, and scenario examples remain distinguishable.
RPO, RTO, durability, performance, independence, snapshot consistency, and recovery are presented as properties to measure, not results already observed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external storage benchmark, CSI conformance run, failure injection, restore exercise, security assessment, or production incident study is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently separates volume persistence, PV/PVC binding, provider topology, access constraints, application replication/fencing, snapshot consistency, independent backup, validated recovery, retention, and physical deletion.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can classify data, choose ephemeral or persistent volume contracts, govern classes, solve topology, interpret modes, design StatefulSet/member lifecycle, fence writers, build backup/restore, expand safely, measure performance, secure copies, and diagnose the exact storage stage without destructive guessing.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from data semantics through volume lifetime, PV/PVC, classes, topology, modes, inventory, StatefulSet identity/retention, replication/fencing, backup/restore, expansion, performance, security, observation, diagnosis, and platform products. Ten examples remain distinct; five exercises progress from class design through unsafe-state audit, recovery engineering, diagnosis, and remote-instrument transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
